title: Scalar naturality of the polynomial-diagonal adjunction reduction
statement:
Let $R\to A$ be a flat finitely presented homomorphism of commutative Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $R\to R'$ be any homomorphism with $R'$ Noetherian. Fix a presentation $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Put $A'=A\otimes_RR'$, $P'=P\otimes_RR'$, $Q=A\otimes_RA$, $Q'=A'\otimes_{R'}A'$, and $p_1(a)=a\otimes1$. Work in ordinary module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with derived tensor [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] and Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Set $C=C_A^P(\Omega^n_{P/R})[n]$ and $C'=C_{A'}^{P'}(\Omega^n_{P'/R'})[n]$, where coinduction has its precomposition action [def-trf-derived-coinduction] and the ordered differential volume identifies the coefficient lines [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials, def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra]. Let $c:C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'\to C'$ be the counit-mate exchange of [lem-sfb-perfect-coinduction-tor-independent-exchange], with this coefficient identification and shift.
For $T\in D(A)$ set $T'=T\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'$, $T_1=T\otimes_{A,p_1}^{\mathbf L}Q$ and $T'_1=T'\otimes_{A',p'_1}^{\mathbf L}Q'$. Suppose $T$ is pseudo-coherent over $A$ [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex] and has finite Tor amplitude over $R$, and $T'$ has the analogous properties over $A'$ and $R'$. Finite Tor amplitude means that derived tensor with any base-ring module has cohomology in a fixed finite interval. The polynomial-diagonal derived reduction of [lem-trf-polynomial-diagonal-rhom-reduction], after the ordered-volume identification, induces natural bijections
$$\rho_T:\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Q)}(A[0],T_1)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(C,T),\qquad
\rho'_{T'}:\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Q')}(A'[0],T'_1)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A')}(C',T').$$
They can be chosen simultaneously with the following specified normalization: $\rho_C$ sends the diagonal class of the normalized polynomial-chart pair on $\operatorname{Spec}A/\operatorname{Spec}R$ [lem-trf-relative-duality-polynomial-chart] to $1_C$, and likewise for $C'$. For every $v:A[0]\to T_1$, with $v'$ its derived extension along $Q\to Q'$ under $A\otimes_Q^{\mathbf L}Q'\simeq A'$ and $T_1\otimes_Q^{\mathbf L}Q'\simeq T'_1$, one has
$$\rho'_{T'}(v')=(\rho_T(v)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A')\circ c^{-1}.$$
This asserts naturality of the whole morphism adjunction for arbitrary $T$ with these properties; it asserts no global sheaf gluing or proper-duality comparison.

source.place: Agent scalar-naturality refinement of Tag 0E2E (lemma-relative-dualizing-noetherian) and the generator assertion of Tag 0E2F (lemma-base-change-relative-dualizing); ordered coefficient normalization of Tag 0BZI (section-relative-dualizing-complex-algebraic), footnote, and Tag 0BZJ (lemma-well-defined). The full naturality square is not stated verbatim in these sources.

proof.text: The coefficient line is free on the ordered volume, so the objects $C,C'$ are the polynomial dualizing objects of [lem-trf-algebraic-shriek-relative-perfect]. In particular they are allowable targets and $\operatorname{End}_{D(A)}(C)=A$, with $a$ acting as $a1_C$, and likewise over $A'$, by taking $H^0$ using [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections]. The primed ring is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]: the base-changed presentation exhibits it as a finite-type $R'$-algebra. Its finite presentation is obtained by extending the finitely many defining relations; its flatness follows directly by identifying $N\otimes_{R'}A'$ with $N\otimes_RA$ and applying [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] to an injection of $R'$-modules. Thus both applications have the required flat finite-type Noetherian hypotheses.

The map $c$ is invertible. Indeed [lem-trf-flat-polynomial-quotient-perfect] makes $A[0]$ perfect over $P$. To verify Tor independence with $P'$, resolve $R'$ freely over $R$. Tensoring that resolution with the $R$-flat modules $P$ and $A$ remains exact by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]; the first tensor is a free $P$-resolution of $P'$, whose tensor with $A$ is the second tensor. Its higher homology vanishes, which is Tor independence by [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. Apply [lem-sfb-perfect-coinduction-tor-independent-exchange] with its rings $(P,A,T)=(P,A,P')$ and coefficient $\Omega^n_{P/R}[n]$. Its counit characterization is precisely the specified $c$, including the ordered coefficient identification.

Choose the affine normalized chart classes $\xi:A\to C_1$ and $\xi':A'\to C'_1$ by [lem-sfb-polynomial-koszul-diagonal-class], with its letter $B$ replaced by our $A$. Multiplication by each class is an isomorphism onto the corresponding derived diagonal Hom; taking $H^0$ by [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] says these Hom groups are free rank one on $\xi,\xi'$. These choices are normalized polynomial-chart pairs as required by [lem-trf-relative-duality-polynomial-chart]: their objects are its displayed polynomial models, their diagonal maps satisfy its pair condition, and their refinement comparisons have its ordered contraction $\operatorname{dual}(t-a)\otimes d(t-a)\mapsto1$. We select these pairs on the two affine schemes; no comparison with an independently chosen global pair is needed. The scalar-extension clause of the Koszul-class node gives the exact equality $c_1\bar\xi=\xi'$, where $\bar\xi$ is the derived extension of $\xi$ along $Q\to Q'$ and $c_1=c\otimes_{A',p'_1}^{\mathbf L}Q'$. Its comparison is the evaluation-counit comparison used in step 2, not an unspecified isomorphism.

source.place: Agent assembly of the specified ordered graph construction underlying Tag 0E2E (lemma-relative-dualizing-noetherian), Tag 0E2F (lemma-base-change-relative-dualizing), and Tags 0BZI/0BZJ (section-relative-dualizing-complex-algebraic, lemma-well-defined).

proof.text: Take $H^0$ of [lem-trf-polynomial-diagonal-rhom-reduction], using [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] on the one-point site. Restriction along $p_1$ retains the underlying cohomology, so this gives $A$-linear bijections $s_T:\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Q)}(A,T_1)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(C,T)$ natural in every allowable $T$. Apply this also at $T=C$, which is allowable by step 1. Steps 1 and 3 identify its source and target as free rank-one $A$-modules with bases $\xi$ and $1_C$. Hence $s_C(\xi)=u1_C$ for a unit $u\in A$: its inverse linear bijection supplies an inverse scalar. Define $\rho_T(v)=s_T(v)\circ(u^{-1}1_C)$. These remain natural bijections induced by the reduction after this fixed normalization, and $\rho_C(\xi)=1_C$. Perform the identical normalization independently over $A'$ to obtain $\rho'$. This defines them simultaneously for all allowable targets.

source.place: Agent degree-zero assembly of the polynomial-diagonal reduction; degree-zero identification: sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08JA (lemma-section-RHom-over-U). Scalar normalization as in duality.tex Tag 0E2W (lemma-uniqueness-relative-dualizing).

proof.text: Naturality in a morphism $f:C\to T$ gives $\rho_T(f_1\xi)=f\rho_C(\xi)=f$, where $f_1=f\otimes_{A,p_1}^{\mathbf L}Q$. Since $\rho_T$ is bijective, for every $v$ we therefore have the explicit inverse formula $v=f_1\xi$ with $f=\rho_T(v)$. The primed formula is identical. This uses naturality between allowable objects only: both $C$ and $T$ have the required properties.

source.place: Elementary naturality of the preceding Hom bijections, evaluated on the chosen universal element.

proof.text:
Extend $v=f_1\xi$ along $Q\to Q'$. Functoriality of derived scalar extension [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor], under the tensor identifications in the statement, gives $v'=(f\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A')_1\bar\xi$. Step 3 gives $\bar\xi=c_1^{-1}\xi'$, so
$$v'=\bigl((f\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A')\circ c^{-1}\bigr)_1\xi'.$$
Apply the primed inverse formula of step 5. This yields exactly $\rho'_{T'}(v')=(\rho_T(v)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A')\circ c^{-1}$. The object $T'$ is allowable by the stated assumption. If $A=0$ or $A'=0$, the corresponding categories and Hom modules have one element; every formula still holds, with the unique identity morphism. For $n=0$ the volume and graph contractions are empty, hence are identities; no sign or positive-dimension assumption entered.

source.place: Elementary application of functoriality to the class equality in Tag 0E2F (lemma-base-change-relative-dualizing), with the counit-mate normalization from step 3.
